uncited: Rasterization Pipeline Optimization refers to the family of algorithmic and hardware techniques designed to accelerate the rendering of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) by reducing the computational overhead of tile intersection, sorting, and alpha compositing.
It solves the bottleneck where standard rasterization overestimates Gaussian extents, processes non-intersecting pixels, and suffers from serial blending latency.

What sets this family apart from sibling methods like [3D Gaussian Splatting Differentiable Rasterizer](2813-3d-gaussian-splatting-differentiable-rasterizer.md) (which focuses on the differentiable math) or [3D Gaussian Splatting MVP](3410-3d-gaussian-splatting-mvp.md) (which focuses on memory layout) is the explicit restructuring of the rendering pipeline stages—specifically moving culling to parallel preprocess phases, replacing coarse bounding-box tests with precise geometric checks, and co-designing hardware units for projection and sorting.
The core optimization principle is the reduction of the "work" performed by the pixel-level render kernel.
**Early Culling:** Moving the determination of Gaussian-tile intersection from the serial render stage to the parallel preprocess stage.
For each splat, copy `center.xyz` as raw float bits to `d[0..2]`.
For non-DC SH coefficients, pack each coefficient's RGB into `RGBA16F` texels (B=0), layout is `[splat0_c1, splat0_c2, …, splat1_c1, splat1_c2, …]`.
SH TBO: `GL_RGBA16F`, 8 B per non-DC SH coefficient per splat.
The optimization of the 3D Gaussian Splatting rasterization pipeline emerged alongside the initial publication of 3DGS [Parent](2812-3d-gaussian-splatting.md).
As 3DGS gained popularity for novel view synthesis and SLAM, the computational cost of rendering millions of Gaussians became a primary bottleneck.
Early implementations used coarse bounding boxes for culling, leading to significant overdraw.
The technique is widely used in real-time rendering applications, SLAM systems (e.g., SplaTAM variants), and neural rendering pipelines where frame rate is critical.
